screens.name: Customer Search
screens.purpose: Check whether the customer already exists by postcode and surname before creating a new record.

screens.name: Customer Details
screens.purpose: Enter the new customer's personal details, address and marketing consent.

screens.name: Documents
screens.purpose: Upload proof of identity for the customer and see the check status of uploaded documents.

screens.name: Review & Submit
screens.purpose: Read-only summary of everything entered so far, with the button that submits the record for approval and locks it.

screens.name: Approval Queue
screens.purpose: List of customers submitted for approval, oldest first, where a Team Lead approves them.

screens.name: Confirmation
screens.purpose: Shows that the customer record has been approved, with the reference number, approver, approval time and welcome email status.

actions.description: Enters postcode and surname and presses Search; matching existing customers are listed below on the same screen
Presses Clear to empty the search fields
Presses Open on a result row to open an existing customer (not shown in the recording)
Presses Create new customer when the customer is not found
Picks the Account type (Personal or Business) from the dropdown
Ticks 'Customer has given marketing consent' only if the customer said yes
Presses Save and continue after filling in the details
Presses Choose File to pick the ID document image or PDF
Picks the Document type from the dropdown
Presses Upload; the document appears in the Uploaded documents table with status Pending check
Presses Submit for approval; the record is locked for editing and appears in the Approval Queue
Team Lead presses Approve on a row with status Awaiting approval (button only shown to the Team Lead role)

journey.description: The onboarding officer enters the customer's postcode and surname and presses Search to see whether the customer already exists.
If the customer is not in the results, the officer presses Create new customer.

The officer fills in the mandatory personal details (first name, last name, date of birth, account type, postcode), any optional contact and address details and the marketing consent tick, then presses Save and continue.

The officer uploads a photo of the customer's ID, picks the document type, presses Upload, and the document sits in the table as Pending check until someone verifies it; then presses Continue to review.
The officer reads through the summary of everything entered and presses Submit for approval, after which the record is locked for editing.
The submitted customer sits in the Approval Queue with status Awaiting approval and an assignee; a Team Lead presses Approve.
The Confirmation screen shows the customer reference number, approver and approval time, and that the welcome email was sent; the officer gives the reference to the customer.

requirement_candidates.statement: As an onboarding officer, I need to search existing customers by postcode and surname before creating a record, so that I do not create a duplicate customer.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Duplicate prevention is the stated purpose of the first screen.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You put in the postcode and the surname and hit Search, and it lists anyone we already have, so you don't create a duplicate.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must show each search result with Customer ID, Name, Date of birth, Postcode, Account type and Status, with an Open button per row.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Inferred from the results table on screen; the expert did not name the columns.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: it lists anyone we already have

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must not save Customer Details unless First name, Last name, Date of birth, Account type and Postcode are filled in.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: First name, last name, date of birth, account type and postcode are mandatory; the rest we fill in when we have it.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must reject a Customer Details save when the postcode is not in a valid UK postcode format.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Hint on screen: 'UK postcode format, e.g. SW1A 1AA'.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: The postcode has to be a valid UK format, otherwise the system won't let you save.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must allow Address line 1, Address line 2, Town / City, Email address and Phone number to be left empty when saving Customer Details.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Expert names the address lines and town as optional; email and phone carry no * on screen.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: The address lines and the town are optional.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must offer Account type as a dropdown with the options Personal and Business.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Account type is a dropdown, personal or business

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must record marketing consent as a tick box that the officer sets only when the customer has actually said yes, and show the answer as Yes/No on the review summary.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Review & Submit shows 'Marketing consent: No' for the unticked box.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: the marketing consent box only gets ticked if the customer actually said yes

requirement_candidates.statement: As an onboarding officer, I need to upload an image of the customer's ID and pick its document type from a dropdown, so that proof of identity is attached to the record.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: We upload a photo of their ID, usually a passport or a driving licence, and pick the document type from the dropdown.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must accept ID document uploads only as PDF, JPG or PNG files of up to 10 MB.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Inferred from the hint under the file control; the expert did not say it.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: We upload a photo of their ID

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must show each uploaded document with status Pending check until it has been checked, and Verified afterwards.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Both statuses are visible in the Uploaded documents table.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: The status column shows pending until the document has been checked.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must list each uploaded document with its file name, document type, upload date and time, and the user who uploaded it.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Inferred from the table columns on screen.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: The status column shows pending until the document has been checked.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must show a read-only summary of all details entered (name, date of birth, email, phone, address, account type, marketing consent, ID document and its check status) before the officer submits.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Review and Submit is a summary of everything so far. You read it through, and if it all looks right you press Submit for approval.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must lock the customer record against editing once it has been submitted for approval.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Also written on screen: 'After submission the record is locked for editing.'
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Once you submit, the record locks and you can't edit it any more.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must allow a team lead to send a submitted record back so it can be edited again.
requirement_candidates.rationale: The expert was not sure; no send-back control was seen on any frame.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You'd have to ask a team lead to send it back, I think.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must list every submitted customer in an Approval Queue, oldest first, showing reference, customer, submitted date and time, submitted by, status and who it is assigned to.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Column list taken from the screen; ordering from the screen subtitle.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Every submitted customer sits here with a status, and it shows who it's assigned to

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must show the Approve action only to users in the Team Lead role; other users can view the Approval Queue but cannot approve.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Also stated in the banner on screen: 'Team leads only. The Approve action is shown to users in the Team Lead role. Other users can view the queue but cannot approve.'
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Only team leads can approve. The Approve button doesn't show for the rest of us, and it says team leads only at the top.

requirement_candidates.statement: When a customer is approved, the system must show a Confirmation screen with the customer reference number, who approved it, when, and the welcome email status.
requirement_candidates.rationale: The reference is what the officer gives to the customer.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: When it's approved, you get the Confirmation screen with a reference number. We give that reference to the customer.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must automatically send a welcome email to the email address entered on Customer Details when the customer is approved.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: A welcome email goes out automatically to the address we entered.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must let the officer print the confirmation and start another customer from the Confirmation screen.
requirement_candidates.rationale: Inferred from the two buttons on screen; the expert did not mention them.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: We give that reference to the customer.

questions.question: What counts as a match in Customer Search: exact surname and postcode, or partial / nearby matches? The results include postcode SW1A 1AB for a search on SW1A 1AA.
questions.why_it_matters: The matching rule decides how well duplicates are caught and what a developer has to build.
questions.context_quote: it lists anyone we already have, so you don't create a duplicate.

questions.question: Must both Postcode and Surname be filled in to search, or can either be left blank?
questions.why_it_matters: Determines search validation and whether a surname-only search is allowed.
questions.context_quote: You put in the postcode and the surname and hit Search

questions.question: What should happen when the officer presses Open on an existing customer, and can a customer with status Closed be onboarded again?
questions.why_it_matters: The Open button and the Closed status were seen but never explained; the team needs to know what path an existing or closed customer follows.
questions.context_quote: it lists anyone we already have, so you don't create a duplicate.

questions.question: What exactly is the UK postcode validation rule (accepted patterns, spaces, upper/lower case) and what error message is shown when it fails?
questions.why_it_matters: A developer cannot implement 'valid UK format' without the precise rule and the failure behaviour.
questions.context_quote: The postcode has to be a valid UK format, otherwise the system won't let you save.

questions.question: Are there validation rules on Date of birth (DD/MM/YYYY only, no future dates, minimum age), Email address and Phone number?
questions.why_it_matters: Only the postcode rule was described; the other fields may also reject bad input.
questions.context_quote: First name, last name, date of birth, account type and postcode are mandatory; the rest we fill in when we have it.

questions.question: Does Save and continue create a saved customer record at that point, and can an officer leave and come back to a half-finished onboarding?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether draft records exist before documents are uploaded and how they show in search.
questions.context_quote: Then you press Save and continue.

questions.question: Who checks uploaded documents and changes the status from Pending check to Verified, and is that done inside this system or elsewhere?
questions.why_it_matters: The verification step is part of the process but nobody on the walkthrough could say who performs it or where.
questions.context_quote: Someone checks them, I'm honestly not sure who, it just changes to verified at some point.

questions.question: What are the full options in the Document type dropdown, and is a proof of address document required as well as the ID document?
questions.why_it_matters: Passport and Proof of address were seen and driving licence was mentioned; the table lists two documents but the form is labelled 'Upload ID document'.
questions.context_quote: We upload a photo of their ID, usually a passport or a driving licence, and pick the document type from the dropdown.

questions.question: What happens when an upload is the wrong file type or over 10 MB, and can an uploaded document be removed or replaced?
questions.why_it_matters: The limit is shown on screen but no error or delete behaviour was seen.
questions.context_quote: We upload a photo of their ID

questions.question: Can a record be submitted for approval, and approved, while its ID document is still Pending check? The record on screen was submitted with the ID still pending.
questions.why_it_matters: If verification must come first, both Submit for approval and Approve need a gate on document status.
questions.context_quote: You read it through, and if it all looks right you press Submit for approval.

questions.question: How does a submitted record get sent back for editing, who can do it, and does that unlock the record and return it to the officer?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert was unsure and no send-back or reject control was seen; without it a mistake after submission cannot be corrected.
questions.context_quote: You'd have to ask a team lead to send it back, I think.

questions.question: How is a submitted customer assigned to a team lead, and what does Unassigned mean for who picks it up?
questions.why_it_matters: The assignment rule affects who sees which work; one row on screen is Unassigned.
questions.context_quote: it shows who it's assigned to, though I've never worked out how it picks the person.

questions.question: Can a team lead reject a record from the Approval Queue, and are there statuses other than Awaiting approval and Approved?
questions.why_it_matters: Only an Approve action was seen; the team needs the full set of outcomes and statuses.
questions.context_quote: Every submitted customer sits here with a status

questions.question: Which users can view the Approval Queue, and do they see all officers' submissions or only their own?
questions.why_it_matters: The banner says other users can view but cannot approve; the scope of what they can see is not stated.
questions.context_quote: The Approve button doesn't show for the rest of us, and it says team leads only at the top.

questions.question: What should happen when the welcome email bounces or no email address was entered: retry, notify the officer, show a failed state on the Confirmation screen?
questions.why_it_matters: Today a bounce goes unnoticed; email is optional on Customer Details, so approvals with no address are possible.
questions.context_quote: If the email bounces it just sort of sits there, nobody gets told.

questions.question: How is the customer reference number (format NW-2026-31365) generated, and how does it relate to the Customer ID (format C-625922) shown in search results?
questions.why_it_matters: Two different identifiers were seen; the team needs to know which is the customer's identity and which is the onboarding case.
questions.context_quote: When it's approved, you get the Confirmation screen with a reference number. We give that reference to the customer.

questions.question: Does the onboarding officer see the Confirmation screen automatically after a team lead approves, or do they have to find the record again?
questions.why_it_matters: The approval happens in a different role, possibly later; the officer needs a way to get the reference to the customer.
questions.context_quote: When it's approved, you get the Confirmation screen with a reference number.
